Rashi on Makkot 8b:10:1.hebrew: חיותיה הוא - ואף זו מצוה על האב ללמדו, דילפינן לה מקרא בפרק קמא דקדושין (דף ל:), דכתיב "ראה חיים עם אשה אשר אהבת" — הקיש אומנות שהוא חיותו לאשה: כשם שאביו חייב להשיאו אשה, כדכתיב "וקחו לבניכם נשים", כך חייב ללמדו אומנות:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:10:1.english: It is his livelihood - This too is a mitzvah incumbent upon the father to teach him, as we derive it from a verse in the first chapter of Kiddushin (30b), for it is written, "Enjoy life with the woman whom you love" — [the verse] equated a trade, which is his livelihood, with a wife: Just as his father is obligated to marry him off to a wife, as it is written, "And take wives for your sons," so too he is obligated to teach him a trade.

Rashi on Makkot 8b:11:1.hebrew: מכה נפש - גבי הורג בשגגה כתיב "לנוס שמה מכה נפש בשגגה":
Rashi on Makkot 8b:11:1.english: One who strikes a person - Regarding one who kills unintentionally it is written: “For one who strikes a person unintentionally to flee there.”

Rashi on Makkot 8b:11:2.hebrew: פרט למכה אביו - שלא חייב גלות אלא למי שהכאתו תלויה בנפש, שאינו חייב עליו גלות אלא אם כן הרגו. יצא מכה אביו, שהוא חייב עליו מיתה בחבורה בעלמא. וקא ס"ד דממעט ליה מגלות אפילו הרגו:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:11:2.english: To exclude one who strikes his father - For [the Torah] imposed exile only on one whose striking is dependent on [the victim's] life, [meaning] that he is liable to it only if he killed him. This excludes one who strikes his father, who is liable to death for a mere wound. And it was initially thought that [the verse] excludes him from exile even if he killed him:

Rashi on Makkot 8b:11:3.hebrew: לרבן שמעון דאמר - בסנהדרין בפ' ד' מיתות (סנהדרין דף מט:) חנק חמור מסייף, ולדידיה ההורג את אביו בחנק, דתנן (שם דף פא.) מי שנתחייב ב' מיתות ב"ד נידון בחמורה, וההורג אביו חייב שתי מיתות, שהעושה חבורה באביו מן הנחנקין הן, והמכה נפש מן הנהרגין, וכאן יש חבורת אביו ורציחה. ולר"ש דאמר חנק חמור, אם היה זה מזיד היה בחנק, ועכשיו שהוא שוגג לא נתנה שגגתו לכפרה בגלות, אם נתנה תורה כפרה לשגגת סייף שהיא קלה, לא נתנה כפרה לשגגת חנק:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:11:3.english: According to Rabbi Shimon, who said - in Sanhedrin, in the chapter [entitled] "Arba Mitot" (Sanhedrin 49b), that strangulation is more severe than the sword. And according to him, one who kills his father is [executed] by strangulation, as we learned (ibid. 81a): One who has incurred two death penalties of the court is judged according to the more severe one. And one who kills his father incurs two death penalties, for one who wounds his father is among those who are strangled, and one who strikes a person fatally is among those who are killed [by the sword]; and here there is both the wounding of his father and murder. And according to Rabbi Shimon, who said that strangulation is more severe: if this [killing] had been intentional, he would be [executed] by strangulation. Now that it is unintentional, his unintentional act was not given atonement through exile — for even though the Torah gave atonement for unintentional [killing punishable by] the sword, which is lighter, it did not give atonement for unintentional [killing punishable by] strangulation.

Rashi on Makkot 8b:13:1.hebrew: ולרבנן דאמרי סייף חמור מחנק, הורג אביו שגגת סייף הוא - שהרי אילו מזיד היה, נידון בחמורה שהיא סייף, ושגגת סייף נתנה לכפרה בגלות:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:13:1.english: And according to the Rabbis, who say that the sword is more severe than strangulation, one who kills his father [unintentionally] has committed an unwitting sword-offense - For had he acted intentionally, he would be judged with the more severe [death], which is the sword; and an unwitting sword-offense is given to atonement through exile.

Rashi on Makkot 8b:14:1.hebrew: רבא אמר - ברייתא היא נמי כדעת רבנן, וההורג את אביו נמי גולה, דשגגת סייף היא. והא דקתני "פרט למכה אביו", לאו להורגו קא ממעיט, אלא בעושה בו חבורה בשוגג:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:14:1.english: Rava said - The baraita, too, [follows the view of] the Rabbis, and one who kills his father is also exiled, since it is a case of unintentional killing by the sword. And that which it teaches, "to exclude one who strikes his father," does not exclude one who kills him, but rather one who inflicts a wound on him unwittingly:

Rashi on Makkot 8b:16:1.hebrew: לוקה דלטייה - ואמרינן [בשבועות] (דף לה.): המקלל את חבירו עובר בלא תעשה, ואתיא ״במה הצד״ מהמקלל דיין ונשיא וחרש (סנהדרין דף סו.):
Rashi on Makkot 8b:16:1.english: He is flogged, because he cursed him - And we say [in Shevuot] (35a): One who curses his fellow transgresses a negative commandment, and it is derived by a "what is the common aspect" argument from one who curses a judge, a leader, and a deaf person (Sanhedrin 66a):

Rashi on Makkot 8b:17:1.english: That he testified against him - that he is liable to lashes.

Rashi on Makkot 8b:2:1.hebrew: לרבות טבול יום - שאם נכנס למקדש, ענוש כרת:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:2:1.english: To include one who immersed that day - For if he entered the Temple, he is liable to karet.

Rashi on Makkot 8b:2:2.hebrew: לרבות מחוסר כיפורים - מאותן טומאות הצריכות קרבן, וטבל והעריב שמשו ולא הביא כפרתו, ונכנס למקדש — חייב. וארבע טומאות הן הטעונות קרבן: הזב, והזבה, והיולדת, והמצורע:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:2:2.english: To include one who lacks atonement - [This refers] to those impurities that require an offering, [where the person] immersed and the sun set on him, but he did not bring his atonement [offering], and he entered the Temple — he is liable. And there are four impurities that require an offering: the zav, the zavah, the woman after childbirth, and the leper.

Rashi on Makkot 8b:2:3.hebrew: מעוד קאמינא - "עוד טומאתו בו", המילה "עוד" קרא יתירא לדרשא הוא:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:2:3.english: From "yet" I was speaking - [I derived it from the verse] "His impurity is yet upon him"; the word "yet" is an extra expression in the verse, [which is there] for a derivation.

Rashi on Makkot 8b:3:1.hebrew: איכא דמתני לה - יש שמשנים להא דא"ל ההוא מרבנן לרבא, והא דאותביה רבינא אהא:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:3:1.english: There are those who teach it - [They teach] this matter that a certain one of the Sages said to Rava, and that which Ravina raised as an objection, with regard to this [baraita]:

Rashi on Makkot 8b:3:2.hebrew: אין צ"ל חריש וקציר של שביעית כו' - דעל כרחך בשביעית דשמיטה הכתוב מדבר, דאי כדכתיב דאיום השביעי קאי, מאי שנא חריש וקציר דנקט? אלא ה"ק: ששת ימים תעבוד ובשביעי תשבות, והששה שאתה עובד בהן בחריש ובקציר תשבות:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:3:2.english: It is not necessary to say plowing and harvest of the Sabbatical Year, etc. - For you are forced [to say] that the verse is speaking of the Sabbatical Year of shemitah; for if it were as written, [that it refers to] the seventh day, what is different about plowing and harvest, that it mentions them? Rather, this is what it is saying: "Six days you shall work, and on the seventh you shall rest" — and in the six [days] in which you work, with plowing and with harvest, you shall rest.

Rashi on Makkot 8b:3:3.hebrew: הנכנס לשביעית - (וחריש של שביעית) שלא יחרוש בששית חרישה המועלת לשביעית:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:3:3.english: That enters into the Sabbatical Year - (and the plowing of the Sabbatical Year) That one may not plow in the sixth year a plowing that is of benefit to the Sabbatical Year.

Rashi on Makkot 8b:3:4.hebrew: וקציר של שביעית היוצא למוצאי שביעית - שאם הביאה שליש בשביעית, מאז היא ראויה ליקצר, ואם קצרה בשמינית, צריך לנהוג בה קדושת שביעית:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:3:4.english: And the harvest of the Sabbatical Year that extends into the conclusion of the Sabbatical Year - For if it brought forth [a third of its growth] in the Sabbatical Year, from then it is fit to be harvested; and if one harvested it in the eighth year, one must treat it with the sanctity of the Sabbatical Year.

Rashi on Makkot 8b:4:1.hebrew: רבי ישמעאל אומר מה חריש רשות כו' - ובשבת קאי. ולהכי נקט חריש וקציר, לומר לך: מה החריש שאני אוסר לך בשבת — חריש של רשות הוא, שאין לנו חריש של מצוה, אף קציר איני אוסר לך אלא של רשות. יצא קציר העומר:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:4:1.english: Rabbi Yishmael says: Just as plowing is optional, etc. - [The verse] is speaking of Shabbat. And therefore it mentioned plowing and harvesting, to tell you: Just as the plowing that I prohibit to you on Shabbat is optional plowing, for we have no plowing that is a mitzva, so too, I prohibit to you only optional harvesting. The harvesting of the omer is excluded.

Rashi on Makkot 8b:5:1.hebrew: אם מצא חרוש אינו צריך לחרוש - אבל קציר, אפילו מצא קצור, מצוה לקצור לשמה, דכתיב ״וקצרתם והבאתם את עומר״:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:5:1.english: If he found [the field] plowed, he need not plow - But with reaping, even if he found [the grain] already reaped, it is a mitzva to reap it for its own sake [i.e., for the purpose of the offering], as it is written: "And you shall reap it, and you shall bring the omer" (Leviticus 23:10).

Rashi on Makkot 8b:7:1.hebrew: לאו מילתא היא דאמרי - שהיה לי להשיבו תשובה נצחת, דקרא לאו במצוה איירי:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:7:1.english: That which I said is nothing - For I should have answered him with a decisive reply: that the verse is not speaking about a mitzvah.

Rashi on Makkot 8b:7:2.hebrew: מאי טעמא קציר דומיא דחריש - מה חריש בכל מקום, מצא חרוש אין מצוה לחרוש, אף קציר בהכי עסקי׳, שאם מצא קצור אין מצוה לקצור. יצא קציר העומר, שאפילו מצא קצור מצוה לקצור:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:7:2.english: What is the reason [that] harvesting is similar to plowing? - Just as plowing, in every place, [if] one found [the field] plowed, there is no mitzvah to plow, so too harvesting — we are dealing with this [type], that if one found [the crop] already harvested, there is no mitzvah to harvest. This excludes the harvesting of the omer, for even if one found it already harvested, there is a mitzvah to harvest [it]:

Rashi on Makkot 8b:7:3.hebrew: ואי ס"ד מצוה - שהכתוב מדבר בקציר של מצוה, האם מצא קצור אינו קוצר? תמיהא היא זו:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:7:3.english: And if it enters your mind [that it is referring to] a mitzvah - [That the verse is speaking] of a harvest that is a mitzvah, [is it so that] if one found [the grain] already harvested he need not harvest? This is astonishing!

Rashi on Makkot 8b:8:1.hebrew: ע"י הבן - אם הרגו לבנו בשוגג:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:8:1.english: Due to the son - If he killed his son unintentionally.

Rashi on Makkot 8b:8:2.hebrew: חוץ מגר תושב - שאין ישראל גולה על ידו:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:8:2.english: Except for a ger toshav - For a Jew is not exiled on his account.

Rashi on Makkot 8b:8:3.hebrew: הכל גולין - מפרש בגמרא לאיתויי מאי:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:8:3.english: Everyone is exiled - The Gemara explains what this comes to include.

Rashi on Makkot 8b:9:1.hebrew: בשוליא דנגרי - בלימוד חרש עצים, שאינו מלמדו תורה אלא אומנות. שוליא יויינד"רינו:
Rashi on Makkot 8b:9:1.english: With a carpenter's apprentice - In teaching woodworking, where he is not teaching him Torah but a trade. Shulya [means] an apprentice (in Old French, vayindrino).

Tosafot on Makkot 8b:1:1.hebrew: טמא יהיה מכל מקום - קשה: לישתוק מ"אשר" ומ"יהיה"? ויש לומר: דאשר אורחיה דקרא הוא:
Tosafot on Makkot 8b:1:1.english: "He shall be impure" in any case - This is difficult: Let [the verse] be silent about [the words] "asher" ("which") and "yihyeh" ("shall be")? And one can say: [The word] "asher" is the normal manner of the verse.

Tosafot on Makkot 8b:3:1.hebrew: אינו צ"ל חריש וקציר של שביעית כו' - תימה: דבשלמא קציר כתיב בהאי ענינא "את ספיח קצירך לא תקצור", אבל חרישה לא כתיב כלל התם. וכ"ת דילפינן מקראי דכתיבי כל שאר עבודות קרקע — הא איכא מ"ד פ"ק דמו"ק (דף ג:) דדוקא אהנך דכתיבי בהדיא מיחייב, אבל אינך לא! וחרישה גופה ממעט התם, מדקאמר: החורש בשביעית אינו לוקה. וי"ל דכיון דקסבר דקציר אתי לתוספת, חריש נמי אתא לתוספת:
Tosafot on Makkot 8b:3:1.english: "It need not say plowing and harvest of the Sabbatical Year," etc. - This is difficult: For harvest, granted, it is written in this subject, "the aftergrowth of your harvest you shall not reap" (Leviticus 25:5), but plowing is not written there at all. And if you say that we derive it from the verses that are written about all the other labors of the land — but there is an opinion in the first chapter of Moed Katan (3b) that one is liable only for those [labors] that are written explicitly, but not for the others! And [the prohibition of] plowing itself is excluded there, from the fact that it says: One who plows in the Sabbatical Year does not receive lashes. And one can answer that since he holds that harvest comes to teach about the additional period [before and after the year], plowing, too, comes to teach about the additional period.

Tosafot on Makkot 8b:5:1.hebrew: דלמא חרישת העומר דמצוה ואמר רחמנא תשבות - קצת קשה: לישתוק מיניה דתשבות, ומהיכי תיתי לן? דהא למישרי מצרכינן קרא! וי"ל דהא לא חייש רק לסתור דרשא דאשמעינן "מה חריש רשות", ומעתה נאמר דאתא לדרשא אחרינא:
Tosafot on Makkot 8b:5:1.english: Perhaps the plowing for the omer, which is a mitzvah, and the Merciful One says "you shall rest" - This is somewhat difficult: Let [the verse] be silent about "you shall rest," and from where would we derive [the prohibition]? For we require a verse in order to permit [it]! And one can answer that [the questioner] was concerned only to undermine the teaching that we derived, "just as plowing is optional," and [if so,] from now on we can say that [the phrase] comes for a different teaching:

Tosafot on Makkot 8b:9:1.hebrew: והא אמרת יצא האב המכה בנו - קשה לר"י: דהיינו דוקא כשמייסרו ומכהו בתוכחתו, אבל אם הלך ביער והורגו בשוגג, למה לא יגלה? וי"ל דמשמע ליה דמיירי בכל ענין, אף אם מכהו לייסרו, דאם לא כן, אמאי נקט טפי בן מאדם אחר:
Tosafot on Makkot 8b:9:1.english: "But didn't you say: 'To exclude a father who strikes his son'" - It is difficult for Rabbeinu Yitzchak: [The exclusion applies] specifically when he disciplines him and strikes him as rebuke. But if he went into the forest and killed him unintentionally, why should he not be exiled? And one can say that [the Gemara] understood that [the mishna] is speaking of any situation, even if he strikes him to discipline him; for if not, why did it specify a son rather than another person?
